content:
mara: Heads up — deploy-bot flagged a p95 token-latency spike on canary for release v3.5.0. Auto-rollback rule fired but paused because EU-dedicated-1 is pinned. Need quick decision: manual rollback of canary or keep pinned traffic? @sudhir @ingrid

deploy-bot: [system] canary telemetry | p95 latency 420ms (threshold 300ms) | error_rate 0.8% | auto-rollback: triggered -> paused (dedicated pin present). dashboard: https://telemetry.internal/release/1767779999

sudhir: I see it too. Correlates with the kv-cache optimization we merged yesterday — TTF (time-to-first-token) bumped a bit in the tail.

ingrid: confirming — the kv-cache hotpath change landed in this rollout. I can toggle the change off on canary nodes (rollback the tweak) and redeploy canary in ~12m.

alex_p: prefer a targeted approach over full revert if possible — dedicated customers pinned could see differences. Which pools are pinned?

mara: EU-dedicated-1 and internal-qa are pinned. No external prod customers are pinned, but EU-dedicated has paying customers behind it.

pmaria: if we do a broad revert we should prep a short customer note. If we keep pinned traffic, still good to prepare comms.

ops_oncall: manual unpin / full rollback of a dedicated pool requires ops checklist + 2FA confirmation. ETA ~20m for safe-run.

sudhir: Proposed plan: 1) revert the kv-cache tweak on canary only and validate. 2) if p95 improves, shift a small percentage of EU-dedicated-1 to fallback variant (v3.4.9) instead of full unpin. 3) prepare release note + support blurb in case we escalate to full revert.

ingrid: I can execute (1) and (2). Will run the rollback commands and post logs. Need greenlight to proceed.

mara: greenlight. Marking manual-rollback-start and looping ops.

deploy-bot: [action] manual-rollback-start initiated by mara at 1767779999. Notifying oncall and watchers.

ingrid: running now:
```
./infra/rollout revert --service=inference --image=v3.4.9 --target=canary
kubectl annotate rollout/inference canary rollback=manual
```
Starting at 1767779999. Will stream checks here.

sudhir: I'll watch telemetry and run diff dashboards for p50/p95/p99.

ops_oncall: acknowledged. prepping routing play for partial shift if canary stabilizes.

[~10 minutes later]

deploy-bot: canary telemetry update | p95 280ms (down) | error_rate 0.2% | auto-rollback cleared.

ingrid: revert on canary finished successfully. Logs: `recreate: 0 failed, 12 pods replaced`. Requesting approval to apply a 10% fallback traffic shift for EU-dedicated-1 to v3.4.9 (keep the pool pinned otherwise).

mara: approved. ops_oncall please apply the routing patch and ack.

ops_oncall: applied routing change: EU-dedicated-1 -> 10% to v3.4.9, 90% still v3.5.0 (pinned). Observability shows p95 now ~290ms. No customer errors surfaced.

alex_p: drafting customer blurb: "We observed increased inference latency during a canary for v3.5.0 after a kv-cache optimization. We reverted the canary and applied a small traffic shift; monitoring shows improvement. No action is required from customers at this time." pmaria to finish and publish.

pmaria: ack — support & status page drafts ready, scheduling the brief for next 15m. Changelog entry: rollback of kv-cache tweak from canary, partial traffic fallback for EU-dedicated-1.

sudhir: follow-ups: 1) add a runtime flag for kv-cache optimization behind an explicit toggle; 2) add a canary-only A/B test for future cache changes; 3) condition our auto-rollback to ignore brief <5min spikes when dedicated pools pinned.

ingrid: I'll open the PR for the toggle and the smaller canary test today.

mara: thanks everyone. I'll update the release notes and close this thread once status page is posted. :thumbsup:

[closing note]
deploy-bot: [log] manual-rollback workflow completed at 1767780600 — canary reverted, partial fallback applied, notifications queued.
